lessons.title: Watch everyone except the ball
lessons.objective: See spacing, gravity and weak-side action in real possessions.

payload.prompt: Why is off-ball action important when analyzing?

options.text: Off-ball movement shows where help comes from and who gets open.
Off-ball action tells you what play the coach called.
Off-ball action means the offense is doing poorly.

explanation.correct: Right. Off-ball movement and cuts reveal defense weaknesses before the ball moves.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Off-ball action is where successful possessions are decided: screens and cuts show why plays work or fail.

payload.prompt: What is the weak-side in a possession?

options.text: The side away from the ball where help defense leaves shooters open.
The side of the court with the worst players.
The side where fouls happen more often.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Weak-side is where help leaves gaps. Smart offenses find weak-side shooters.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The weak-side is opposite the ball. Help defense leaves it open, creating opportunities.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Watch the weak-side forward, she is cutting before the pass.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: The forward is moving without the ball, anticipating a pass or screen.
The forward is on defense.
The forward is fouling someone.
The forward just caught the ball.

payload.translation: She is pointing out that the forward uses off-ball movement to anticipate the play and get open.

followUps.line: That is why they are so hard to defend.
followUps.why: Recognition that unpredictable off-ball action makes defense harder.

followUps.line: Their weak-side is always open because of that.
followUps.why: A good follow-up understanding that skilled off-ball movement creates mismatches.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Watching off-ball action shows you how the offense works before the ball gets there.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: The spacing was too tight, so help collapsed on the driver.

payload.question: What happened?

options.text: The shooters were bunched together, so help could reach the driver without leaving anyone open.
The ball handler made a mistake.
The defense was playing man-to-man.
The shooter made a three-pointer.

payload.translation: She means her team's shooters stood too close together, so a helper only had to take a step to stop the driver and nobody was left open.

followUps.why: Recognition that spacing is a choice the offense controls.
Good follow-up understanding that spacing works best with quick cuts.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Good spacing pins defenders to their shooters. Cramped spacing lets one defender help on the drive and still get back.

lessons.title: Named sets: horns, Spain, elevator
lessons.objective: Recognize horns, Spain pick-and-roll and elevator screens.

payload.prompt: Match named offensive sets to how they work.

pairs.definition: Two bigs stand at the elbows and either can set a ball screen for the guard at the top.
A ball screen where a third player also sets a back screen on the screener's defender.
Players move continuously reacting to defense with screens, cuts and passes.

distractorDefinitions: A defense that only plays man-to-man.
A system where the ball handler never passes.

explanation.summary: Horns and Spain are named sets with set positions. Motion is a principles-based system where players read the defense and keep moving.

payload.prompt: Match screening concepts to what they set up.

pairs.definition: Two screeners stand side by side, the shooter runs between them, and they close like doors behind him.
Four players form a square around the lane: two on the blocks and two at the elbows.
Back-to-back screens by two players for one player running off them.

distractorDefinitions: A defensive formation with all five in a line.
A passing pattern used in the fast break.

explanation.summary: An elevator screen is two screeners closing together on a shooter; a stagger is two screens one after the other; a box set is a formation, not a screen.

payload.prompt: Tap where horns set screeners stand.

diagram.alt: Half-court diagram. Half-court line at the top, baseline at the bottom, hoop near the baseline. Regions marked: left elbow, right elbow, left corner, top of the key.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Horns has screeners at both elbows.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Horns has screeners at the elbows, high on the court.

payload.prompt: In a Spain pick-and-roll, where does the roller finish?

diagram.alt: Half-court diagram. Half-court line at the top, baseline at the bottom, hoop near the baseline. Regions marked: the rim, the top of the arc, the left wing and the left sideline.

hotspots.label: Pops to the top of the arc

explanation.correct: Yes. The roller dives to the rim. The extra back screen on the roller's defender is what makes Spain hard to guard.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The roller dives to the rim while a third player screens the roller's defender. That back screen is the Spain twist.

payload.prompt: Why do teams run horns against zone?

options.text: The elbows attack the soft gaps in zone defense.
Horns only works against man-to-man.
Horns guarantees a three-pointer.

explanation.correct: Right. Elbows in horns hit zone gaps where coverage is thin.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Horns targets zone gaps at the elbows where coverage struggles.

payload.prompt: What does an elevator screen do?

options.text: Two screeners close together behind a shooter who cuts between them.
Scores a layup by dunking.
Traps the ball handler.

explanation.correct: Exactly. The two screeners open like elevator doors, let the shooter slip through, then shut on his defender.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. An elevator screen is two screeners side by side who close together behind a shooter so his defender cannot follow.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Their motion offense is hard to defend because everyone cuts at the right time.

payload.question: What is she saying?

options.text: A flexible system where players read the defense and keep cutting and screening.
The team only runs set plays.
The team passes once per possession.
All players are point guards.

payload.translation: She means the team uses motion principles: players react to defense with timely cuts and screens.

followUps.line: They never run the same play twice.
followUps.why: Good recognition that motion adapts rather than follows rigid sets.
Good follow-up understanding that motion requires ball movement.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Motion offense is players reading defense and cutting/screening at the right time, not rigid sets.

lessons.title: Advanced pick-and-roll defense
lessons.objective: Tell apart tag, top-lock, scram and peel switches.

payload.prompt: Match pick-and-roll defenses to how defenders react.

pairs.definition: The ball handler's defender stays on his top side and fights over the screen.
A defender briefly touches the roller to slow the dive, then recovers to his own man.
A quick swap on the fly to fix a mismatch, so a big ends up back on a big.

distractorDefinitions: Fouling the ball handler to stop play.

explanation.summary: Top-lock fights over the screen, a tag slows the roller for a moment, and a scram switch fixes a mismatch on the fly. Teams use these names loosely, so ask a fan what they saw.

payload.prompt: What is a peel switch in pick-and-roll defense?

options.text: The roller's defender peels off onto a ball handler who turns the corner, and the two defenders swap men.
A switch at half court.
A switch that only happens after a made basket.

explanation.correct: Right. The big peels off the roller to stop a guard who is getting downhill, and the guard picks up the roller.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. In a peel switch the roller's defender peels off onto the ball handler who turned the corner, and the defenders swap men.

payload.prompt: When is late switch used in pick-and-roll defense?

options.text: After the screen is set, once the roll or the pull-up would otherwise be open.
A switch that always leads to a foul.
Switching only at possession end.

explanation.correct: Exactly. A late switch is a reaction: defenders fight the screen first and swap only when the roll would be open.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. A late switch happens after the screen is already set, so the defenders swap only when an easy roll or pull-up is about to appear.

payload.prompt: What is the risk of top-lock defense?

options.text: If the handler gets around the screen, the roller's defender has to stop two players.
Team always gets fouled.
Top-lock has no risks.

explanation.correct: Right. Fighting over the screen keeps the handler in front, but if he slips past, one defender suddenly has two players to stop.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Every coverage has a trade-off. Top-lock keeps the handler in front, but if he gets past, the roller's defender is stuck guarding two players.

lessons.title: Gravity and the passing big
lessons.objective: Explain hub offense and why shooters bend a defense.

payload.prompt: What does gravity mean in strategy?

options.text: Scorer pulls defenders toward him, leaving other teammates open.
Effect of gravity on the ball during a shot.
A foul that pulls players together.

explanation.correct: Right. Gravity is how a scorer's ability commands defense, opening lanes for others.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Gravity is how a dangerous scorer pulls defense toward him.

payload.prompt: Why is a passing big valuable to modern offense?

options.text: Big at elbow sees whole floor and kicks out to open shooters when help comes.
Passing bigs can only score dunks.
Passing bigs are not valuable.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Passing big at hub sees all cuts and kick-outs from center.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Passing big creates gravity and reads defense from middle.

payload.prompt: What is hub offense?

options.text: Offense run through center or high-post player who reads cutters and shooters.
Offense that only shoots three-pointers.
Offense that drives to basket every play.

explanation.correct: Right. Hub offense centralizes ball through skilled passer in middle.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Hub offense puts passing big in middle as decision maker.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: When he touches it, defense collapses and teammates get open threes.

payload.question: What is she describing?

options.text: Player's gravity: defenders converge on him, leaving shooters unguarded.
A foul being called.
A turnover happening.
A bad pass.

payload.translation: She means the star commands so much attention that when he catches the ball, multiple defenders move toward him, leaving teammates open.

followUps.why: Recognition that gravity works best with space between shooters.
Good follow-up understanding that gravity needs shooters.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Gravity is when defenders collapse on scorer, leaving shooters open. Works best with good spacing.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Their passing big runs offense from elbow and defense cannot stop it.

payload.question: What makes them effective?

options.text: Big at elbow reads cutters and kick-outs because he sees whole floor.
The big scores every possession.
Defense is fouling too much.
The big only shoots threes.

payload.translation: She means the offense runs through a versatile big who has playmaking ability. From the elbow he can pass, score or shoot.

followUps.why: Recognition that big who can pass AND shoot is dangerous.
Good follow-up understanding that hub needs active off-ball movement.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Passing big at elbow runs offense by making reads. If he can shoot, defense is in trouble.

payload.prompt: Your passing big has three fouls. What does the coach do?

situation.narrative: Early in the third quarter, the offense runs through the big at the elbow. He picked up his third foul on defense.

facts.label: Big's foul status
facts.value: Three fouls, most of the game still to play

facts.label: Offensive identity
facts.value: Built around this player's passing from the elbow

options.label: Keep the hub, and protect him on defense
options.consequence: The offense keeps its engine, and he guards a quieter player and avoids risky rim help.
considerations: Fouls come on defense, so the fix belongs on defense
Passing from the elbow does not add fouls
He stays available for the fourth quarter

options.label: Sit him for a few minutes, then bring him back
options.consequence: He is safer, but the offense loses its hub for a stretch of a close game.
considerations: A rest can make sense if the game is getting away
The backup cannot replace his passing
A short stretch beats a long one

options.label: Stop running the offense through him
options.consequence: The offense gets worse and he is no less likely to foul on defense.
considerations: Giving up the hub does nothing about defensive fouls
It wastes his best skill

payload.expertNote: Fouls are a defensive problem. Coaches usually protect a foul-troubled star on defense and keep using his offense.

lessons.title: Series schemes: drop vs switch vs zone
lessons.objective: Follow why a team changes coverage or goes zone as a surprise.

payload.prompt: Why switch from drop to switch coverage in a series?

options.text: Guards were pulling up over the big in drop, and switching takes that space away.
Drop defense is always better than switch.
Team ran out of plays.

explanation.correct: Right. Drop gives a shooter room to pull up behind the screen. If it keeps hurting, a team may switch, at the price of mismatches.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Teams move off drop when shooters keep pulling up in the space behind the screen. Switching removes that space but can create mismatches.

payload.prompt: What is a zone change-up in a series?

options.text: Switching from man-to-man to zone to confuse offense.
Changing all five players at once.
A change-up pitch in baseball.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Zone change-up is surprise defensive adjustment forcing offense reset.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Zone change-up means showing zone when opponent expects man-to-man.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: They packed the paint so tight no one could get to rim.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: Defense crowded inside, making it impossible to score near basket.
Offense scored too many points.
A player got injured.
Referee made a bad call.

payload.translation: She means defense packed multiple players into the paint, making driving very difficult.

followUps.line: That is why they were shooting threes.
followUps.why: Good recognition that packing paint forces outside shooting.

followUps.line: Only works if you defend the three.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that packing paint opens corner threes.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Packing paint means multiple defenders inside. Stops drives but opens corner threes.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Game 4 they switched to zone and totally threw us off.

payload.question: Why was this an adjustment?

options.text: Team expected man-to-man so zone was surprise disrupting their reads.
Zone defense is illegal.
They fouled more in zone.
Zone defense always loses.

payload.translation: She means the other team showed zone when her team expected man-to-man. Adjustment caught them off guard.

followUps.why: Recognition that zone needs different off-ball movement than man.
Good follow-up understanding that defensive adjustments happen constantly.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Zone change-ups are adjustments that disrupt offense expecting man-to-man. Need counter-adjustment.

lessons.title: Shot creation and touch
lessons.objective: Name the footwork, fakes and touch that separate scorers.

payload.prompt: What is shot creation?

options.text: Ability to get open for shot using footwork, fakes and moves without set plays.
Referee creating a shooting foul.
Making a three-pointer.

explanation.correct: Right. Shot creation is improvising and getting your shot off against defense.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Shot creation is ability to generate offense and get your shot through moves.

payload.prompt: How is pump fake used in shot creation?

options.text: Fake a shot so the defender jumps or leans, then drive or shoot.
Pump fake always results in made shot.
Pump fake is same as step-back.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Pump fake freezes defender, then shooter drives or rises over him.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Pump fake makes defender jump or overcommit, creating space.

payload.prompt: Fill in shot-creation terms and moves.
payload.template: A scorer who keeps attacking the paint and forces the defense to collapse applies {{pressure}}. Faking a shot, then stepping under the defender's raised arms, is the {{move}}.

explanation.correct: Perfect. Rim pressure is a player's threat to attack the basket, and the up-and-under is a fake-then-step-under move that beats a defender who jumps at the fake.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Rim pressure is how often and how hard a player attacks the basket. The up-and-under is the fake-then-step-under move, not a crossover or a screen.

payload.prompt: Match shot-creation concepts.

pairs.definition: Fake shot (pump) then drive or step under defender's raised hands.
Softness and finesse of layups and floaters; high-touch scorers finish difficult angles.
A player's threat to attack the basket, forcing the defense to collapse or foul.

explanation.summary: The up-and-under beats a defender who bites on a fake. Touch is finishing skill. Rim pressure is the constant threat of a drive.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He is best shot creator because he gets his shot off anytime.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: He has footwork and skills to score without relying on teammates or plays.
He shoots more than anyone else.
He is the tallest player.
He runs every play.

payload.translation: She means this player has strong shot creation: footwork and fakes that let him create space in contested situations.

followUps.line: That is why he is so hard to defend.
followUps.why: Recognition that shot creation makes player dangerous in isolation.

followUps.line: He uses different moves every time.
followUps.why: Good follow-up understanding that good shot creators are unpredictable.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Shot creation is having footwork and fakes to get your own shot off without much help.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: He has such soft touch around rim, even awkward angles go in.

payload.question: What is she complimenting?

options.text: His skill at finishing layups with soft, controlled shot touch.
His ability to block shots.
His passing accuracy.
His rebounding.

payload.translation: She means the player has exceptional finesse around the rim. He can make layups from difficult angles because of his soft touch.

followUps.why: Recognition that touch and finesse are hallmarks of elite scorers.

followUps.line: Hard to guard a shot like that.
followUps.why: A warm remark that shows you get why touch is so hard to defend.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Touch is softness and finesse of layups. Great touch means making difficult finishes.

lessons.title: Diagnose a possession like a coach
lessons.objective: Explain why a possession worked or failed in one sentence.

payload.prompt: Ball-screen at top, defender drops, roller gets ball, help comes, turnover. What went wrong?

situation.narrative: Pick-and-roll where roller was open but could not finish.

facts.label: Roller action
facts.value: Caught the pass, then lost the ball

facts.label: Help defense
facts.value: The weak-side defender left the corner shooter and stepped in

options.label: The roller should have kicked it to the open corner.
options.consequence: Yes. The helper left a shooter open, and the quick pass out was the read.
considerations: Help that leaves a shooter gives away a good look
Forcing a finish into two defenders is the turnover risk
The pass out beats the rotation

options.label: The spacing was tight, so the helper did not have to leave far.
options.consequence: Not here. The corner shooter was wide open, so the floor was spaced well enough.
considerations: A wide-open shooter means spacing did its job
The mistake came after the catch

options.label: The screener set a bad screen that blocked the roller.
options.consequence: No. The roller got the ball, so the screen worked.
considerations: A weak screen affects the catch, not what happens after it
The roller caught it cleanly

payload.expertNote: Diagnose a possession by asking who was left open. Here the answer was the corner, and the ball did not get there.

payload.prompt: Forward gets pass on wing, pump-fakes and defender jumps, then forward misses step-back three. What was wrong?

situation.narrative: Good shot creation move but final shot was poor.

facts.label: Alternative
facts.value: Could have driven to rim or kicked to corner

options.label: Took bad shot instead of driving or passing.
options.consequence: Right. Pump-fake opened floor, but step-back three was low-quality.
considerations: 27-foot step-back worse than rim or corner three
Good shot creation ended in poor shot selection
Needs smart decision-making after creation

options.label: Pump-fake was not effective.
options.consequence: Wrong. Pump-fake worked; defender was out of position.
considerations: Defender bit and was open
Issue is what happened after, not fake

options.label: Teammates were not in right spacing.
options.consequence: Possibly. Poor spacing could close off drive or corner.
considerations: If teammates not spaced, drive is tougher
But a 27-foot step-back is rarely the best look
Shot creation is half skill; decision-making matters

payload.expertNote: Great shot creation is not just getting open; it is finishing with the best available shot.

payload.prompt: Off-ball action: weak-side cutters run staggered screens, one gets free for open three. What worked?

situation.narrative: Possession where off-ball movement resulted in excellent shot.

facts.label: Ball handler
facts.value: Did not hold ball; moved quickly

facts.label: Cutter movement
facts.value: Multiple cutters and screens forced defense to work

facts.label: Weak-side use
facts.value: Attacked weak-side where help was not

options.label: Off-ball movement and spacing created open shot.
options.consequence: Correct. Staggered screens and weak-side attack forced defense to break.
considerations: Cutter was free because defense pulled elsewhere
Spacing made help impossible
Good off-ball execution creates easy outcomes

options.label: Ball handler made amazing pass.
options.consequence: Partly true. Pass was clean but cutter already open.
considerations: Pass finished it, but cutter was already open
Off-ball movement did heavy lifting
Bad passer could still work with good spacing

options.label: Defense made mistake and left him open.
options.consequence: Unlikely. Good offense forces mistakes; this was designed.
considerations: Offense executed well
Good off-ball action often looks like defensive mistakes

payload.expertNote: Diagnose by watching ball and off-ball play. Good teams generate easy shots through spacing and movement.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: That possession worked because everyone moved at same time.

payload.question: What is she observing?

options.text: Coordinated off-ball movement created open shot, not individual talent.
The ball moved too slowly.
The defense fouled someone.
One player scored a lot.

payload.translation: She recognizes offense succeeded because players were synchronized: cuts, screens, passes in rhythm.

followUps.line: That is what good coaching looks like.
followUps.why: Recognition that synchronized offense is a coach's system.
Good follow-up understanding that coordinated movement is fundamental.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Good possessions work through synchronized off-ball movement and spacing, not individual talent.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: That pick-and-roll failed because roller had nowhere to go when help came.

payload.question: What is she diagnosing?

options.text: Poor spacing left roller without kick-out option when defense collapsed.
The roller was fouled.
The screener set bad screen.
The defense played zone.

payload.translation: She means offense's spacing was poor, so when help collapsed, roller had no open teammate.

followUps.why: Recognition that spacing cures help-defense collapses.
Good follow-up understanding that execution also matters.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: When pick-and-roll fails due to help, diagnose whether it was spacing, delayed pass, or panicking.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Defense adjusted second half and that play is not working anymore.

payload.question: What is she recognizing?

options.text: Defense changed coverage; offense needs to counter-adjust with new reads.
The offense is playing worse.
The referee is making different calls.
It is a different team.

payload.translation: She means defense made adjustment (different coverage or positioning) that disrupts a play that worked in first half.

followUps.why: Recognition that adjustments are part of strategy.
Good follow-up understanding that it is back-and-forth.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: When good play stops working mid-game, defense has adjusted. Offense needs counter-adjustments.

payload.title: Reading a possession
payload.setting: Your friend says a possession was bad, but you think it was a good read that did not convert.

exchanges.theirMessage: That was a terrible possession. He should not have taken that shot.

replies.text: I think the read was solid even though it did not work out.
replies.theirResponse: Maybe you are right, he was open.
replies.coachNote: You separated decision quality from result quality.

replies.text: Yeah, that was awful. He should have passed.
replies.coachNote: You agreed without analyzing the actual possession.

exchanges.theirMessage: The spacing was bad so he had no kick-out option.

replies.text: Good catch on spacing, or maybe he needed to pass quicker?
replies.theirResponse: Yeah, both are issues. The pass was slow.
replies.coachNote: You identified multiple diagnosis points without being preachy.

replies.text: That is just bad offense. They cannot execute.
replies.theirResponse: Whatever, you do not understand possession analysis.
replies.coachNote: You dismissed analysis without engaging with the actual basketball.

payload.closingNote: Diagnosing possessions means separating the decision from the result and looking at spacing, reads and execution.
